data.narrative:
Teradar is a Series B defense and security technology company founded by MIT-trained leadership (CEO Matt Carey) and deep domain expertise in terahertz sensing and chip architecture. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of ten peers across the Defense & Security sector: two public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and eight private firms including Dream Security, Harmattan AI, Code Metal, Defense Unicorns, and Heven AeroTech.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression, using $175M in total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, implies a valuation of $332M. Peer-median analysis across six same-stage, same-sector comparables yielded a median valuation of $1.1B, with a range spanning $300M to $3.0B. The peer set includes Dream Security at $3.0B (high outlier), Harmattan AI at $1.4B, Code Metal at $1.2B, and Defense Unicorns and Heven AeroTech each at $1.0B.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $283M (low) to $1.3B (high), with a median of $729M. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around comparable company selection and stage-specific multiples in the defense technology sector, where milestone achievement, regulatory pathway clarity, and customer traction variation drive outsized valuation divergence at Series B.
